messages.content: Madison is off my plate. I need to look at Arizona next. The Phoenix metro training week is still squishy, and I’m considering tacking on Sedona with Mark if it doesn’t make the work week weird.

Sure. Let’s build a provisional plan and keep the risky pieces visible. What do you know so far: first required time and city, the clinic locations, the last in-person obligation, when Mark could arrive, and how long you’d want in Sedona?

Monday 2 p.m. setup at a reference lab in Tempe. Tuesday and Wednesday clinic sessions may split between Scottsdale and Mesa, order TBD. Thursday is either a Glendale wrap-up or a remote debrief. If we do Sedona, Friday to Monday is my thought. Mark could fly into Phoenix Thursday night or maybe Friday morning.

Given a Monday 2 p.m. setup, I’d be careful about flying in Monday unless you are very comfortable with a morning arrival and no disruption. Would you rather arrive Sunday and settle in? Also, should the work hotel be central to the Tempe/Mesa/Scottsdale triangle, or closer to whichever site ends up being first?
I’d rather go Sunday. Afternoon from Denver is better than a morning scramble, and nonstop should be easy to Phoenix. United or Southwest are fine; don’t pick a worse schedule just for the airline.

For your outbound, I’d rank it: 1) Sunday early-afternoon United nonstop DEN-PHX, arriving midafternoon; cleanest for check-in and a normal evening. 2) Southwest midafternoon nonstop; also fine, with the bag/change flexibility trade-off and no assigned seats. 3) A later low-fare nonstop; cheaper, but it turns Sunday into a late arrival. For the Sedona version, the return should be a Monday early-to-mid-afternoon PHX-DEN nonstop so you can drive down from Sedona with buffer.
For Mark, is Thursday night or Friday morning smarter?

Thursday night is the better experience if his workday allows it. Even if Glendale is in person and ends around 4, you could get back toward Tempe, regroup, and pick him up at PHX that evening. Friday morning may be cheaper, but it burns the start of your Sedona day and creates more waiting around Phoenix. I’d only choose Friday if Thursday becomes too late or too expensive.
That’s what I’m thinking. For the work hotel I want practical. No resort fee drama, and I don’t want to move midweek unless there’s a real reason.

Work-hotel shortlist: 1) Tempe suite property: strong guest score, free parking, fridge, pool, hot tub, and fitness access; best central anchor for Tempe and Mesa, acceptable for Scottsdale and Glendale. 2) Scottsdale hotel: closer if Tuesday is Scottsdale, but resort fees and paid parking make it less clean. 3) Airport hotel: useful only for a late arrival or very early departure; worse for the clinic loop. I’d hold the Tempe suite through Friday checkout while the schedule firms up.
Tempe suite property sounds right. Rating over 4 is fine, and I’d use the pool or gym after training. Hot tub is a plus after being on my feet. Please note quiet king and fridge.

I’ll use that as the work-hotel target. For Sedona, I’d compare three types: 1) West Sedona resort-style hotel with a strong rating, pool, hot tub, fitness room, and cancellable king rooms where balcony can be requested. 2) Uptown/boutique option with better walkability and some balcony-view rooms, but weaker workout or hot-tub setup. 3) Village/Bell Rock option with a lower rate and good amenities, but less of the classic Sedona-room feel. My first choice is the cancellable West Sedona option if Mark is likely.
Yes, don’t lock us into a nonrefundable view room. What about the car? I’ll be driving between those sites, then probably up to Sedona.

I’d pick up at PHX Sunday and keep one vehicle through Monday. A compact or midsize sedan is enough for work-only, but it gets less appealing with two people, bags, and Sedona heat. Midsize SUV is the balanced choice. Standard SUV is more comfortable if Mark brings hiking gear or you want easier cargo space. If reimbursement stops Friday, it is still cleaner to split the cost than swap cars mid-trip.
Midsize SUV may be enough, but if Mark comes Thursday with hiking stuff I can see standard being easier. What schedule questions do I need answered before I push approvals?

Ask for: the exact Tempe setup address; the Tuesday/Wednesday site order; whether Thursday is definitely Glendale or remote; the Glendale address and target end time; whether any Friday debrief, gear return, or materials shipment is expected; and whether you need to carry anything bulky. Separately, get Mark’s latest workable Thursday flight and the Sedona cancellation deadline.
Give me the provisional recommendation in order. I need something I can paste into my notes.

Ranked plan: 1) Full extension plan: Erin flies Sunday afternoon nonstop DEN-PHX, stays at the Tempe suite hotel Sunday through Friday, keeps one midsize or standard SUV, Mark flies in Thursday evening, Sedona Friday to Monday, both return Monday early-to-mid-afternoon nonstop. Best overall if Thursday ends by about 4. 2) Hedge plan: book only cancellable hotels and your flight now, wait on Mark and Sedona until Thursday is confirmed. 3) Work-only plan: Tempe hotel, return Thursday evening or Friday morning, no Sedona. Use this only if Glendale or Friday obligations stay uncertain.
Use #1 as the working plan. Mark can answer tomorrow. I’m going to ask the coordinator now—can you word the questions so I don’t sound like I’m planning vacation on their time?

Send this: To finalize travel, can you confirm the Monday Tempe setup address and time, the Tuesday and Wednesday clinic locations and order, and whether Thursday will be an in-person Glendale wrap-up or remote debrief? If Glendale is in person, what end time should I plan around? Also, is there any Friday debrief, equipment return, or bulky material I should account for in the rental car? For Mark: If you can take a Thursday evening DEN-PHX nonstop, we can keep the Sedona weekend intact; Friday morning is cheaper but cuts into the day.
One more: I do not want to discover later that the good flight home is a red-eye or some annoying connection. Build around a sane Monday return if we do Sedona.

Agreed. For the Sedona version, I’d only use a Monday PHX-DEN nonstop leaving early-to-mid afternoon. That gives you breakfast in Sedona, a buffered drive to Phoenix, fuel and rental return time, and no late-night arrival. Next decision once Mark confirms: your Sunday afternoon outbound, his Thursday evening inbound, the shared Monday return, Tempe suite hold, cancellable Sedona hold, and SUV class.

messages.content: Coordinator came back. Monday setup is Tempe at 2, Tuesday Scottsdale, Wednesday Mesa, Thursday Glendale in person but they expect to wrap by 4. No Friday debrief. Mark can do a Thursday evening flight or a cheaper Friday morning one. I’d like to book before the Sedona cancellable rate disappears.

Great, that makes the extension workable. I’d book your Sunday afternoon nonstop to Phoenix, Tempe suite hotel through Friday checkout, Mark’s Thursday evening nonstop, Sedona Friday to Monday, and one shared Monday nonstop home. The two remaining choices are Mark’s arrival and SUV size. Thursday costs more than Friday, but preserves the whole Sedona Friday.
Let’s compare Mark one more time. If Thursday lands too late, I don’t want a miserable pickup.

Thursday option: after-work nonstop, landing around 8 p.m. local, about $120 more than Friday. You would finish Glendale, head back toward Tempe, then pick him up without rushing dinner. Friday option: cheaper morning nonstop, but you either wait near Phoenix or get to Sedona closer to midday or early afternoon. I’d take Thursday unless his workday slips.
Book Thursday. For mine, use the Sunday afternoon nonstop that lands with enough time to check in and not the late budget flight.

Selected: your Sunday early-afternoon DEN-PHX nonstop, arriving midafternoon, and Mark’s Thursday evening DEN-PHX nonstop. For the shared return, I’m holding a Monday early-afternoon PHX-DEN nonstop. I’ll request a window for your solo outbound; for the shared return, do you want adjacent seats prioritized over window seats?
Yes. On the return, together matters more than both windows.

Car choice: midsize SUV is the cheaper balanced option; standard SUV is more comfortable for two bags, hiking gear, and summer driving, and both hotels have parking covered. I’d choose standard SUV if Mark is bringing trail gear, with midsize SUV as the fallback if inventory gets tight.
Standard SUV, with midsize SUV as fallback. No sedan unless there’s no choice and you ask me.

Hotels are ready to confirm: Tempe suite property Sunday through Friday checkout, quiet king away from elevator, fridge, free parking, pool, hot tub, and fitness room. Sedona Friday through Monday, cancellable king room, balcony/high-floor request, pool, hot tub, and fitness access. The cancellable Sedona rate expires tonight. Lock it?
Yes, lock the cancellable Sedona room. Don’t pay for a guaranteed view if it makes the rate nonrefundable.

I’ll book the cancellable room and add balcony/high-floor as a request only. For payment split: work card for your airfare, Tempe hotel, and the work portion of the rental; personal card for Mark’s flight, Sedona, and the weekend portion. If the rental has to stay on one card, I’ll note the work-versus-personal split in the itinerary.
That split works. Use the same cards as last time.

Booked. Summary: you have a Sunday afternoon DEN-PHX nonstop; Mark has a Thursday evening DEN-PHX nonstop; you both return Monday early afternoon PHX-DEN nonstop. Tempe suite hotel is confirmed through Friday checkout with quiet king, fridge, free parking, pool, hot tub, and fitness room. Sedona is confirmed Friday to Monday on the cancellable king rate with balcony/high-floor request. Standard SUV is booked from PHX Sunday to Monday, with midsize SUV fallback noted. Seats requested: window on your solo outbound, adjacent seats together on the shared return.
What remains before I can stop poking at this?

Only operational items: get the exact Glendale address, recheck seat maps at check-in, confirm Mark’s bag count, and save the Sedona cancellation deadline. Calendar timing: land Sunday midafternoon; Monday setup at 2 p.m.; Tuesday Scottsdale; Wednesday Mesa; Thursday Glendale ends around 4, then airport pickup; Friday checkout and drive to Sedona after rush hour; Monday leave Sedona by about 9:30 for PHX, fuel, SUV return, and the early-afternoon flight home.

messages.content: Five days out and Arizona is doing the last-minute thing. Mark’s inbound moved 50 minutes later, the return aircraft swap split our seats, Tempe says the hot tub is closed, Sedona says balcony is still request-only but they’ll sell me a guaranteed first-floor patio, and the rental app is warning limited SUVs. What actually needs changing?

Not much needs changing. Keep Mark’s flight, but treat Thursday as airport pickup plus snacks, not dinner. Keep Tempe unless the commute matters less than the hot tub, which I don’t think it does. Decide whether the patio upcharge is worth it, fix the return seats, and protect the SUV reservation.
Keep Tempe. Annoying about the hot tub, but I’m not moving to a worse commute and paid parking. What do you think on the Sedona patio?

I’d skip the paid patio if it is only first-floor access and not a view guarantee. With heat and possible smoke, balcony time may be limited anyway. Keep the king room with high-floor/balcony request and ask again at check-in.
Agreed. On seats, take the one window and the adjacent aisle if that keeps us together. Keep my outbound window if it’s untouched.
Your outbound window is still set. For the Monday return, only one nearby window remains; do you want that assigned to you or Mark?
Give Mark the return window. I’ll take the aisle next to him.

Done. Rental plan: keep the standard SUV reservation, check in online before you fly, and go to the desk if the app offers a downgrade. Accept a midsize SUV or crossover only with a rate adjustment confirmed; decline a sedan unless you approve it.
Last thing: heat and smoke. I don’t want a rigid hiking plan.

Use an early-and-flexible plan: Friday drive up and do only an easy overlook; Saturday start at sunrise and be off exposed trails by 10, with Tlaquepaque, Chapel area, pool time, or a spa slot as backups; Sunday choose a shorter creek or scenic-drive option if haze is bad. Pack N95s, electrolytes, sun sleeves, and extra water for the SUV. Monday leave Sedona by 9:00-9:30, fuel near Phoenix, return the SUV, and recheck seats at check-in.
